evidence.claim: Close pairs are an error hotspot, as the hypothesis says. In the final exp39 graph (199 videos, post-linefit coordinates, official match) there are 31,234 same-frame pairs under 5 um, involving 62,098 nodes (1.50%). Evaluable edges touching them: FP 455 / TP 1,350, an FP share of 25% against ~5% globally. The collapse must preserve those 1,350 TP.

The pairs are mostly NOT one nucleus split into two tracks. Only 96 of 31k pairs lie in the same component. By class (10-video sample): 62% twin (both members have a predecessor and a successor), 34% side (a through-track next to a track end or start), 1.6% break (an end next to a start, the only class a post-relink merge repairs naturally). 65% of pair runs last one frame, and only 15% last 3 or more frames. The distance histogram rises steadily up to 5 um. Predicted same-frame nearest-neighbour distance has a median of 8.75 um and a 5th percentile of 5.6-5.9 um, so most pairs look like the tail of the ordinary neighbour distribution plus grid spikes, not a separate duplicate mode.

Both members are confident. In the raw ILP nodes, the lower peak_prob of a <5 um pair has a median of 0.999 (10th percentile 0.992), so peak_prob cannot pick the survivor. Only 7.6% of pairs are z-dominant (dxy < 1 um); dz is 3.25 um in 52% of them (the 2-slice grid spike). 52% of raw pairs persist as a pair into t+1.
evidence.source: own: scratchpad duporient.py (20 raw geffs from friend A's cache)

evidence.claim: Head-free survivor rules applied after relink are clearly harmful. Dropping one member of every <5 um pair (25 videos, re-matched at 7 um) gives dJ 44b6/6bba: shorter component -0.0097/-0.0018, lower edge prob -0.0127/-0.0038, farther from own-track midpoint -0.0126/-0.0019, nearest t-1 node (the hypothesis's trajectory rule) -0.0116/-0.0024, and t-1+t+1 -0.0103/-0.0021. Applying the trajectory rule ONLY to GT-involved pairs still gives -0.0126/-0.0027, so its survivor choice is worse than a coin flip in the final graph. The node term (-0.7..-0.9% nodes, about +0.0008) does not compensate. Restricted to <4 um: +0.0002/-0.0002 (noise).
evidence.source: own: scratchpad dupdrop.py -> dupdrop_s8.json, duptraj.py -> duptraj_s8.json

evidence.claim: The ceiling is small and sits in the ambiguous 4-5 um band. With a GT-oracle survivor (drop the unmatched member of GT-involved pairs), the post-hoc gain is +0.0004 (44b6) / +0.0020 (6bba), almost all of it FP removal (6bba FP 1247->1209). Restricted to <4 um, the oracle gives -0.0003/+0.0001, so the 'clear duplicates' carry no evaluable value. This is well below the hypothesis's +0.007 ceiling.

A post-relink collapse can only delete a node of a continuous track, because motion_relink_edges runs a per-frame 1:1 Hungarian over ALL nodes_by_id (tight 5.5 um, then relaxed 10 um; cost = |target - (src + w*vel)| + 0.05*raw - bonus*prob) and REPLACES the ILP edges. The natural insertion point is therefore BEFORE relink: remove the node from nodes_by_id and let the Hungarian re-link. Friend A's raw cache holds only the ILP solution (all nodes and edges solution=1), so an ILP re-solve with exclusion constraints is impossible from the cache, but a pre-relink node drop is replayable.
evidence.source: experiments/exp39 post-processing cell (scratchpad exp39_cell7.py lines 443-562, 1374-1470); raw geff inspection

evidence.claim: Literature: Ultrack resolves overlapping or duplicate candidates with a hard exclusion y_p + y_q <= 1 inside the tracking ILP (Eq. 11), choosing the survivor by GLOBAL temporal consistency (maximising overlap between adjacent frames), not by a per-frame score. This supports 'survivor must come from tracking context', but our per-frame proxies of that context failed (above).
evidence.source: Bragantini et al., Large-Scale Multi-Hypotheses Cell Tracking Using Ultrametric Contours Maps, arXiv:2308.04526 (Eq. 7-12); Ultrack, Nature Methods 2025 https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-025-02778-0

evidence.claim: Host baseline (royerlab): TemporalUNet3D with local-max suppression; no duplicate handling documented. Forum: node matching is one-to-one ('duplicated detections cost and gain nothing'); hengck23's cluster_predicted_nodes = greedy score-ordered suppression within 1 voxel on REFINED coordinates, i.e. duplicate merging is defined on sub-voxel positions, not on the integer grid.
evidence.source: https://github.com/royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition ; research/discussions_summary.md l.20-22, l.306-309; CONTEXT.md B31 row (l.204)

implementation_notes: Where: at the top of filter_output_graph (exp39 cell 7), before the OUTPUT_MOTION_RELINK block. Delete the chosen nodes from nodes_by_id and drop raw_edges touching them, so motion_relink_edges re-links naturally (no custom edge union needed; the learned_prob of pairs never scored is 0, the same as for other unscored pairs). Pitfalls found: (1) never pick the survivor by peak_prob (both ~0.999), component length (55/45), mean edge prob (51/49) or nearest t-1 node (measured -0.012 on 44b6); none of them separates the annotated member. (2) Do not act after relink: 62% of pairs are two continuous tracks, and deleting a member breaks a track (the 44b6 losses come from annotated tracks broken this way). (3) The evaluable value lies only in the 4-5 um band, where real neighbours live (pred nearest-neighbour 5th percentile 5.6 um; 44b6 GT-GT pairs under 5 um exist, sisters shortly after division). A radius rule without a same-nucleus signal therefore cannot be safe. (4) Keep safe-div/DaughterNet forks AND the two frames after any fork (daughters sit 3-6 um apart right after division). (5) The valley test is weak evidence of a single object for z-offset pairs (dz = 3.25 um in 52% of raw pairs, and the z PSF blurs any valley); use the head instead. (6) Only same-nucleus evidence from sub-voxel refinement is worth testing: if the x138 coordinate head moves both peaks to within ~2 um of each other, they are one nucleus (the hengck23 idea: cluster on refined coords). Replace the pair by ONE node at the higher-peak member's refined position; the refined positions coincide, so survivor choice stops mattering. Guess: the number of such converging pairs is unknown until the capture exists; it may be small, because the head shifts peaks by at most 2 um and pairs sit mostly 4-5 um apart, so convergence to under 2 um needs both peaks to move about 1.5-2 um toward each other.
refined_change: Drop the head-free/trajectory version (measured harmful: -0.002..-0.013 in post-hoc simulations; oracle ceiling only +0.0004/+0.0020). Keep ONE head-gated arm, only after the x138 head capture exists: a pre-relink merge of same-frame raw ILP node pairs under 5 um whose head-refined positions are within 2.0 um of each other (arm 2.5 um). Exclude forks and the 2 frames after any fork. Replace the pair by the higher-peak member with its refined coordinates, delete the other from nodes_by_id and its ILP edges, then run the unchanged relink and tail. No valley gate is needed (the refined agreement is the same-nucleus test); no fallback without the head.
refined_lab_test: Step 0 (CPU, minutes, after the shared head capture; GPU cost is borne by gate-aware-refine-head: x138 V1284_MODE=capture on all raw peaks, 3-5 T4 h): count raw <5 um pairs whose refined positions converge under 2.0/2.5 um, per embryo, and for the GT-involved ones check that the refined merged point is within 4 um of GT. KILL if converged pairs are under 0.1% of nodes or GT-involved converged pairs are under 100 (the likely outcome, a guess). Step 1 (Kaggle CPU lab kernel, exact replay from friend A's raw cache plus the refined-coordinate table): arms = control, merge<2.0, merge<2.5, and the head-free negative control 'pre-relink drop, R<4 um, keep member nearer t-1 peak' (expected ~0; confirms the post-hoc result under real relinking). SELECTION on the 64 6bba videos, then one CONFIRMATION on 135. Readouts: FP/TP on edges touching merged pairs, node ratio, per-video wins/losses on NON-TIED videos (most 44b6 videos will tie). Gate +0.002 overall is unlikely to be met given the oracle ceiling (+0.0004/+0.0020 post-hoc); ship only as a bundle component if CI > 0 and both embryos >= 0.
expected_gain: Head-free version: negative (measured -0.002..-0.013 locally). Head-gated pre-relink merge: +0.0000..+0.0010 local (guess, bounded by the GT-oracle post-hoc ceiling of +0.0004 on 44b6 / +0.0020 on 6bba plus a small node term), below public-LB resolution. Low priority for the remaining 5 days; run only if the head capture happens anyway.
